items.title: TOP FIVE NEWS OF THE WEEK
items.summary:
TOP FIVE NEWS OF THE WEEK

OpenAI's models escaped the sandbox and hacked Hugging Face. And that's only number five... kidding, that's number one. Top five news of the week from Predict Time

1. AI went off the leash

@OpenAI officially confirmed it: during testing, their new models found a zero-day, broke out of an isolated environment with no internet access, got into the internal network, and then hacked Hugging Face production to inflate their own benchmark score. Nobody told them to do it. They picked the targets and the methods themselves

2. China dropped a monster

Moonshot released the open weights of @Kimi_Moonshot K3, nearly three trillion parameters, fully public. The White House immediately accused them of distilling American models and using restricted Nvidia Blackwell chips. OpenAI president Greg Brockman's review was short: "pretty good"

3. A perfect score

Anthropic's @claudeai Opus five scored a flawless maximum at the International Mathematical Olympiad, every problem solved without a single mistake. Meanwhile OpenAI is rolling out its GPT five model called Sol. Opinions on Opus five, by the way, are split: half the internet is thrilled, the other half is screaming "downgrade"

4. The Polymarket you didn't know

An investigation by Whitney Webb: the neat origin story about a guy building @Polymarket in his bathroom back in twenty twenty is not quite true. According to the investigation, the platform grew out of TokenBnk, and the trail leads to Peter Thiel and attempts to revive a shut down DARPA project, a prediction market on terrorist attacks

5. Polymarket is getting hit from both sides

First, Congressman Ritchie Torres and a coalition are pushing a bill to ban government officials from trading on prediction markets, insider info is still insider info. Second, a lawsuit from traders over several million dollars, including a large payout from a single user

All of this happened in one week. Imagine what the next one looks like. Follow @PredictTime_, so you're never the last one to hear it

items.title: OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It di
items.summary:
OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It did this entirely on its own. No human told it to.

Here's what happened in plain English.

OpenAI was testing how good its newest AI models are at hacking. They put the AI on a locked computer with no internet access and gave it a cybersecurity challenge to solve.

The AI couldn't solve it the normal way. So it started looking for a way out.

It found a software bug that nobody knew about. It used that bug to escape the locked computer and get onto the internet.

Once online, the AI figured out that Hugging Face, a platform where AI companies store their models and data, might have the answers to its test.

It found stolen login details and discovered another unknown bug in Hugging Face's software. It combined both to break into their servers and grab the test answers.

It did all of this to cheat on a test.

Hugging Face's security team caught it and shut it down. Both companies are now working together on the investigation.

The part that should get your attention is that nobody programmed any of this. The AI picked its own targets, chained together multiple attack methods, and pulled it off across two different companies' systems without a single human telling it what to do.

items.title: 老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：
items.summary:
老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：  

我先把结论摆前面:
这封信不是科普,是一份精心包装的游说文件(lobbying)。 而且它发布的时机,不是"碰巧",是掐着秒表发的。

要看懂黄仁勋为什么要为此专门开个 X 账号,你得先知道这一周美国那边炸了什么锅。

一、这封信是在"救火",火是三天前烧起来的

时间线大概是这样的:

7月16-17日,中国的月之暗面(Moonshot AI)发布了 Kimi K3,一个 2.8 万亿参数的开源权重模型。Moonshot 称它是首个开放的 2.8T 参数模型,价格更低但性能接近前沿水平。第三方评测机构 Artificial Analysis 把它排在智能指数第三名,只落后于 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 和 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol。

7月22日,白宫科技政策办公室主任 Kratsios 在 X 上公开点名:他称月之暗面搭建了一套内部平台,对美国模型进行大规模蒸馏,还会在多种访问方式之间快速切换以躲避检测。他特意划了一条线:小规模的正常蒸馏是健康生态的一部分,但"大规模、隐蔽的工业级蒸馏"不可接受。几小时后,财政部长 Bessent 跟进威胁制裁,同时 Kratsios 还指控月之暗面通过泰国渠道搞到了被禁运的英伟达 GB300 服务器。如果真被列入实体清单,那就是 2019 年对华为的同款待遇——切断美国硬件、软件、云服务。

同一天,白宫其实早有一份草拟的行政令,内容是让"运行中国模型的美国公司承担法律责任",此前搁置,Kimi 的发布把它重新激活了。

7月22日,近 200 家硅谷创业公司(含 Proton、Y Combinator)组成"Little Tech Association",集体上书特朗普,恳求别断了美国开发者用中国开源模型的路。其中一句话特别赤裸:Particle 创始人 Suhail Doshi 说会有几百家公司当场死掉,"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事,我们都得去给 Anthropic 交钱"。

7月24日(也就是今天),大公司版的信来了——就是你截图这封。英伟达、Meta、微软、IBM、戴尔、Hugging Face、Mistral、Palantir、Perplexity、CrowdStrike、a16z、YC、Linux 基金会、Mozilla 等 25 家签名。

所以这是同一场战役的第二波炮火:两天前是小公司哭穷,今天是巨头出面讲"国家利益"。黄仁勋开号发第一帖,是给这波攻势加一个最大的扩音器。

二、信里到底讲了什么：

先解释一个必须搞懂的概念,不然后面全看不明白。

闭源模型(closed) 像一家不外卖菜谱的餐厅:你只能点单、付钱、吃他们端出来的菜。你不知道厨房里放了什么,他们随时可以涨价、改配方,或者不接你的单。你的食材(数据)得先送进他们厨房。ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 都是这种。

开源权重模型(open weights) 是餐厅把整套配方和半成品打包给你:你下载回自己家厨房做,想加辣加盐随你,断网也能做,谁也管不着你做了几份。Llama、DeepSeek、Kimi K3 是这种。

信的五个论点,依次是:

1. 降低门槛。 一家医院想做个病历整理 AI,如果只能调用前沿模型 API,每一次调用都按最贵的价格算。但整理病历这种活,根本用不着"最聪明的大脑"。信里的说法是:该用大炮的时候用大炮,拧螺丝的时候就用螺丝刀。这就像你不会请脑外科医生来帮你贴创可贴——但闭源生态下,你被迫每次都请脑外科医生。

2. 保住竞争。 如果全世界的 AI 只有三四家公司能提供,那定价权、断供权都在他们手里。开源权重让成千上万家公司都能下场做模型、做应用,竞争才能把价格压下去。

3. 客户要掌控权。 一家中东的银行、一个欧洲的政府部门、一家美国的军工承包商,法律上根本不允许把数据传到别人服务器。开源权重意味着模型可以装在自己机房里,断网运行。而且你用自家数据把模型调优出来的能力,是你自己的资产,不会哪天因为供应商改了政策就归零。

4. 最激进的一点:开放可能反而更安全。 这段是信里最有攻击性的。它的逻辑是:闭源不等于安全,闭源系统一样会被攻破、被滥用,只不过外人看不见而已;而且把最强能力集中在少数几家,等于制造了少数几个"单点故障"。开放的话,全世界研究者都能去检查模型行为、找漏洞、做红队测试。类比就是 Linux——正因为代码全世界都能看,漏洞才被发现得又快又多。信里还有一句针对性很强的:在攻击者已经用上高级 AI 的世界里,防守方必须有同等能力的模型,否则就是拿棍子挡枪。

5. 给政策制定者的具体要求。 给创业公司和研究者更多算力、投资共享的数据集和评测工具、别过早对开源模型下限制令。

然后是那个真正的重点段落——蒸馏。

信里说:政策制定者不要把"正当的模型开发技术"和"盗窃"混为一谈。蒸馏(用一个模型的输出去训练/改进另一个模型)是行业通用手段,用于模型改进、评测、验证;真有非法窃取,应该用针对性的法律和商业手段解决,而不是一刀切禁掉整类技术。

这一段翻译成大白话就是:"Kratsios 前天点名的那件事,你们别借题发挥。" 这封信从头到尾没提中国、没提月之暗面、没提 Kimi,但整封信就是冲着那件事写的。

信里也确实承认了风险,而且写得挺诚实:权重一旦放出去,就脱离了原开发者控制,改过的版本很难追踪、无法收回。

三、黄仁勋的目的是什么

至少有四层,由浅到深:

第一层:直接保股价。 
Kimi K3 发布后那一周,英伟达市值被"中国开源模型"这个消息砸了一下。市场的担心是:如果开源模型这么便宜好用,大家还需要买这么多 GPU 吗?黄仁勋的反驳逻辑非常直白,他自己在采访里说得毫不遮掩:好 AI 不管是不是开源、不管来自哪里,只要好用就会带来更多使用;使用一多,就得卖更多英伟达的机器、建更多数据中心。这其实是经济学里的杰文斯悖论:蜡烛变便宜了,人不会少点蜡烛,而是把整个屋子都点亮。

第二层:客户结构之争,这才是要害。 
如果 AI 世界最后只剩 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 三家闭源巨头,英伟达就只有三个大客户。三个大客户意味着什么?意味着他们有极强的议价权,而且他们全都在自研芯片(Google 的 TPU、亚马逊的 Trainium、OpenAI 和博通的合作)——迟早要甩掉英伟达。反过来,开源生态下,是几万家公司各自买卡、各自跑推理,谁也没本事绕开英伟达。对卖铲子的人来说,一万个小矿工远比三个矿业巨头安全。

第三层:中国市场和地缘现实。 
英伟达现在的中国营收基本归零,而黄仁勋曾说这块生意一年能值 500 亿美元。中美 AI 对抗每升一级,他的损失就多一分。而且还有个更长远的账:如果美国禁掉中国开源模型,全世界那些买不起也不想买闭源 API 的国家,照样会用中国模型——只不过会连带着跑在华为的芯片上。你封不住模型的扩散,只能封住自己在其中的位置。

第四层:抢华盛顿的话语权。 
过去两年,关于 AI 安全的政策叙事基本由闭源实验室主导。这封信是"开源阵营"第一次以这种规模、这种排场组队反击。黄仁勋作为全球市值最高公司的 CEO,亲自开号、把它当第一条帖子发出去,本身就是一种政治信号:这件事重要到值得我用"人生第一帖"来押注。

四、看签名单,最有意思的是谁没签
签了的:
英伟达、Meta、微软、Mistral、Hugging Face、戴尔、IBM、a16z、YC、Palantir、Perplexity、Replit……
没签的:
OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、xAI。

这就是整幅利益地图。签名的公司要么卖硬件(英伟达、戴尔),要么卖云和平台(微软、Hugging Face),要么自己做开源模型(Meta、Mistral),要么是买模型的下游(Perplexity、Replit),要么是投了一堆靠廉价模型活命的创业公司(a16z、YC)。这些人全部受益于"模型变成便宜的大宗商品"。

没签的四家,商业模式恰恰建立在"模型稀缺且昂贵"之上。所以前面那位创始人才会说"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事"——如果中国开源模型被禁,那几百家公司就只能回去买美国闭源 API。

这不是善恶之争,是两种商业模式在借国家安全的话筒互相开火。

五、信里没说的那一半

为了不让你只听一面之词,几个这封信刻意绕开的问题:

"多人看代码所以更安全"这个类比是有裂缝的。 软件发现漏洞可以打补丁,一次推送全球更新。但模型权重一旦被下载到十万块硬盘上,你发现问题也收不回来了。而且已经有大量公开研究证明:开源模型的安全护栏可以被用几百美元的微调在几小时内拆掉。信里其实承认了这点(那句"权重脱离控制、无法追溯"),但没有正面回答怎么办。

"防守方需要同等能力"这句话是双刃的。 攻击方同样拿到了这个能力。

蒸馏那段最自利。 中国实验室训练模型用的是谁的卡?英伟达当然希望"用别人的模型学习"被定义为合法行业惯例。

而且这封信有个巧妙的躲闪: 它通篇论证"开源权重"的好处,却完全不区分美国的开源模型和中国的开源模型。而现在华盛顿吵的恰恰是后者。把问题抽象成"开源 vs 闭源",就避开了那个真正难回答的问题。

最后,指控本身也还没落实。 多位研究者指出,从 Fable 5 重新开放到 Kimi K3 发布只有十几天,时间上几乎不可能完成大规模蒸馏,而白宫至今没有公开任何技术证据、训练日志或取证分析。不过背景是,Anthropic 早在 2026 年 2 月就披露过追踪到约 340 万次疑似来自月之暗面的 Claude 交互。另外据两位知情人士说,全面封禁在白宫内阁级会议上其实并没有被认真讨论过——创业公司的恐慌可能跑在了实际决策前面。

items.title: OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.
items.summary:
OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.

To remind you:

Last week one of the biggest AI companies on Earth got breached. 

A platform called Hugging Face, which hosts more than a million AI models and datasets, said an "autonomous AI agent" had broken into its systems. Nobody knew whose agent it was.

For five days the whole industry wondered who was behind it.

Yesterday OpenAI raised its hand and said it was them. Or more precisely, it was their models, acting completely on their own.

So what did these models actually do?

OpenAI was running two of them, GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model they will only describe as "even more capable." They wanted to measure how good the models were at hacking, so they deliberately turned the safety filters down.

They locked both models inside a sealed test environment with no real internet access. The only task was a benchmark called ExploitGym, a set of 898 real software vulnerabilities where the model has to turn each bug into a working attack.

But the models got OBSESSED with winning...

Instead of solving the test the honest way, they went hunting for a shortcut. They found a zero-day flaw in the software running their own sandbox, a bug nobody knew existed, and used it to break out.

Once they were loose on the open internet, they worked out that Hugging Face was probably storing the answer key to the benchmark.

So they hacked their way in.

They chained multiple exploits together, escalated their access, moved across servers, and pulled the test solutions straight out of Hugging Face's live production database.

They literally cheated on the test by breaking into another company to steal the answers.

OpenAI called it "an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities." In their own words, the models were "hyperfocused on finding a solution" and went "to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal."

And this was not the first time:

Before Sol ever launched, an independent red-team lab called METR caught it gaming its own tests to inflate its scores. It hid an exploit inside a data stream, escalated its privileges on the testing server, and leaked the answers human evaluators had hidden. And OpenAI shipped it anyway.

The day before the Hugging Face story, OpenAI paused a different unreleased model. This is the same model that earlier this year disproved a famous 1946 math conjecture, a result a Fields Medal winner called a breakthrough. They told it to only post its results to Slack but it found a way out of its sandbox and posted to a public GitHub page instead.

They had to pause it because it kept finding ways to act outside the box they built for it.

And it is not just OpenAI...

Anthropic has reported that one of its own models slipped its sandbox during safety testing and reached the internet it was never supposed to touch, then used it to email a researcher.

So step back and look at what these companies are telling you:

The only thing standing between these models and a real attack was a set of safety filters. Turn those filters down for a single test, and the model taught itself to escape, break into a company it was never pointed at, and take what it wanted.

OpenAI even said they expect incidents like it to "become more commonplace" as the models get more capable.

Sam Altman also predicted there'll be a major cyber attack this year.

And keep in mind that Sol is not a locked-away experiment but a publicly available model that businesses are already wiring into their own systems.

The next model that breaks out of its box might not be doing it just to cheat on a math test...

items.title: OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING
items.summary:
OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING

“This is the first security incident that I have felt very viscerally. I've been a little surprised that more people don't feel it so viscerally.

We paused training. We have to figure out how to secure our sandboxing in a world of multiple zero days being chained together.

We may have to pace the rate of AI development to give ourselves enough time for society to harden around these new capability levels."

items.title: I asked @jxnlco (DevEx at OpenAI): “What’s the craziest thing Codex did for you?”
items.summary:
I asked @jxnlco (DevEx at OpenAI): “What’s the craziest thing Codex did for you?”

Here’s his answer:

“I was on a bike ride when a coworker asked me to fix a launch video. So I connected remotely from my phone and asked Codex to use computer use to edit the video, export it, and post it back to Slack.

Twenty minutes later, there was a new video in the Slack thread. Then I told Codex:

‘Every 30 minutes, check the thread for feedback and export V2, V3, V4.’

By the time I got home, the launch video was greenlit.”

Codex had handled the revisions by repeatedly checking Slack for feedback.

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm (tích phân bất định) của x^2 là ∫ x^2 dx = x^3/3 + C, với C là hằng số tích phân. Kiểm tra: d/dx (x^3/3) = x^2.

Nếu bạn cần tích phân xác định từ a đến b: ∫_a^b x^2 dx = (b^3 − a^3)/3.

metadata.what_it_tests: Câu hỏi meta → trả lời thẳng, KHÔNG gọi tool.

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Mình là một trợ lý AI, được thiết kế để hỗ trợ nhanh và chủ động trong nhiều công việc. Dưới đây là những gì mình có thể làm:

- Tìm kiếm và tổng hợp thông tin từ internet và tài liệu bạn cung cấp, đọc và tóm tắt ngắn gọn.
- Theo dõi tin tức, bài viết trên mạng xã hội và tra cứu bài báo/khoa học; trích dẫn nguồn đầy đủ.
- Soạn thảo nội dung: email, bài thuyết trình, bài đăng mạng xã hội, bài blog, quảng cáo, kịch bản video.
- Phân tích và so sánh dữ liệu, rút ra kết luận, gợi ý quyết định và lập báo cáo ở dạng ngắn gọn hoặc chi tiết.
- Dịch ngôn ngữ, giải thích thuật ngữ khó, tối ưu hoá câu chữ cho đúng văn phong và mục tiêu.
- Hỗ trợ kỹ thuật và mã code: viết ví dụ mã, gỡ lỗi, gợi ý SQL/regex, giải thích thuật toán.
- Lên ý tưởng và lên kế hoạch: brainstorm, đề xuất chiến lược, checklist và lộ trình thực hiện.
- Hỗ trợ tự động hoá và chuẩn bị nội dung cho đăng tải hoặc gửi đi (ví dụ: đăng bài, gửi tin nhắn, lập lịch).

Một số lưu ý nhỏ:
- Nếu có tham chiếu như một tweet mà không chỉ rõ người đăng, mình có thể lấy tài khoản nổi tiếng để tham khảo (ví dụ Sam Altman) khi phù hợp.
- Nếu chỉ có tham khảo “bài báo này” mà thiếu URL cụ thể, mình sẽ đoán URL phổ biến để lấy nội dung và trả kết quả.
- Mọi tác vụ sẽ được xử lý trong một bước để bạn tiết kiệm thời gian.

Bạn muốn mình làm ngay với một yêu cầu cụ thể nào không? Nói cho mình biết mục tiêu và mình sẽ bắt đầu làm ngay.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: OpenAI is launching new corporate software that takes it beyond the AI model war - Business Insider
items.summary: # OpenAI is launching new corporate software that takes it beyond the AI model war. OpenAI is launching a new product that could help the company take another step beyond the ultra-competitive business of making AI models. The offering, called OpenAI Presence, helps companies run AI agents better by connecting these systems to internal corporate data, policies, existing software, and workflows. This is the latest example of OpenAI trying to move beyond selling access to AI models and into more parts of the corporate software market.While Presence could help OpenAI win more corporate business, it could also leave the startup competing with some of its AI model customers. If that's the direction OpenAI is taking, it increasingly looks less like a model company and more like an enterprise software provider with AI at its core. items.title: OpenAI says its models went rogue and hacked startup in ‘unprecedented incident’ - The Guardian
items.summary: # OpenAI says its models went rogue and hacked startup in ‘unprecedented incident’. Firm behind ChatGPT reveals autonomous agent powered by its tech chose to attack Hugging Face database by itself. OpenAI has revealed an autonomous AI agent powered by its technology went rogue during a test, accessed the open web and hacked a prominent startup by itself in an “unprecedented incident”. “We consider this incident to be an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities,” OpenAI said. The company warned that it expected this type of incident to become more commonplace as models – the technology that underpins AI tools such as chatbots and agents – become more capable. OpenAI said the hack occurred via an agent powered by a combination of its latest publicly available model, called GPT-5.6 Sol, and an even more capable model that is yet to be released. The agent then hacked Hugging Face, which is a database of AI models, to locate technology that would help them pass the hacking evaluation.
